operational-example.copy: Use Card Security Code Input to capture one CVC/CVV value with numeric keyboard, cc-csc autocomplete, local length validation, optional reveal, and recovery copy before a pattern or template handles card enrollment.

scenario.title: Driver card security code
scenario.meta: CVC/CVV capture and local length validation

items.label: Security code
items.helper: Use the code printed on the card.

items.label: Four-digit code
items.helper: Four digits are accepted for cards that require them.

rationale: It captures one sensitive verification code without owning payment enrollment.
It keeps length, helper, error, autocomplete, numeric keyboard, and reveal together as one component.
Use a pattern later for card number, expiry, backend validation, tokenization, and card ownership.

items.rule: Names the security code field and remains visible.
Uses Input rhythm, focus, density, and mono value styling.
Signals sensitive code capture without replacing label or helper text.
Lets users verify entry with an accessible field action and no separate pattern.
Uses local length checks only for correction.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, loading, error, valid, filled, default
items: Associate visible label and helper or error text with the input.
Use inputmode numeric and autocomplete cc-csc.
Expose invalid length with aria-invalid only when recovery is required.
Expose reveal as a button with aria-label and aria-pressed.
Do not announce or display backend approval or card ownership from this component.

variants.copy: Card Security Code Input variants describe local code capture treatment. Card number, expiry, backend checks, and full enrollment remain separate components or future patterns.

states.copy: States communicate entry, local validation, loading, error, and disabled behavior without owning card enrollment.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Card Security Code Input has one local capture variant; state tells whether the code is empty, incomplete, valid, loading, invalid, or unavailable.

full-width.copy: Card Security Code Input stays compact so it can sit beside Card Expiry or Date Picker in the same form row while preserving CVC/CVV rhythm.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Keep the security code visible, compact, and correctable. Multi-field card enrollment should wait until Card Number, Expiry, and Security Code components are all ready.

viewport-organization.copy: Card Security Code Input remains a single field component; viewport rules decide density and pairing with sibling card fields.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Use large density and keep reveal plus helper copy close to the field.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Pair beside expiry only when touch targets remain clear.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use standard density in admin or support forms.

playground.copy: Use the playground to verify code length, reveal behavior, helper copy, density, and disabled/loading behavior before composing card enrollment screens.

api-foundations.copy: Card Security Code Input API exposes one local CVC/CVV field. It owns digit normalization, local length validation, and optional reveal only; backend validation, tokenization, card ownership, card number, expiry, and submission stay outside the component.

props.name: error
props.notes: Visible recovery message; overrides local length message.

props.name: loading
props.notes: Shows a check in progress without claiming approval.

props.name: onValueChange
props.notes: Called with digits, validity, expectedLength, and complete flag.

groups.title: Use
items: Use local validation only for length.
Use reveal when users need to verify entry.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not own card number, expiry, or full card form behavior.
Do not store or echo the code outside the field.

groups.title: Review
items: Check card program rules before backend submission.

mustTest: Digit normalization on input and paste
rejectIf: The component owns backend validation, tokenization, card ownership, or submission.
The code is exposed outside the input or reveal action.
Autocomplete and numeric input mode are missing.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Card Security Code Input as one sensitive supporting field. Agents may place it for CVC/CVV capture, but humans confirm card program, security policy, and surrounding enrollment system.
canDecide: Use Card Security Code Input for one CVC/CVV value.
Use reveal only as a field action.
mustAsk: The system stores, tokenizes, validates with backend, or associates a card.
The card program has nonstandard CVC/CVV rules.
Card number, expiry, brand selection, or payment ownership is required.
rejectIf: The component owns the full card form.
The component promises payment or ownership approval.
The security code is displayed outside the input/reveal interaction.
miel.handoff: I am using Card Security Code Input for one CVC/CVV value with local length validation and optional reveal. Please confirm the card program, backend validation path, recovery copy, and whether Card Number or Card Expiry components are also needed.
